claims.text: AlCoFeNi is an example of an initially homogeneous, single-phase BCC solid solution.
Demanding mechanical loading causes a nominally single-phase high-entropy alloy to undergo phase decomposition.
Phase decomposition of the single-phase alloy produces secondary phases.
The secondary phases produced by decomposition are brittle.
The secondary phases preferentially nucleate or precipitate at grain boundaries.
High mechanical stresses accelerate local atomic diffusion.
High mechanical stresses destabilize the uniform solid solution.
Grain-boundary secondary phases act as crack-initiation sites.
The formation of brittle grain-boundary phases lowers fracture toughness.
The formation of brittle grain-boundary phases promotes brittle fracture during further loading.
Mechanically loaded samples will have a higher volume fraction of secondary phases than unloaded controls.
Mechanically loaded samples will have a coarser distribution of secondary phases at or near grain boundaries than unloaded controls.
Mechanically loaded samples will exhibit lower fracture toughness than the untested baseline.
Mechanically loaded samples will exhibit lower ductility than the untested baseline.
The as-cast, homogeneous single-phase baseline has high toughness and ductility under standard mechanical tests.

The proposed behavior applies during substantial cyclic or high-rate loading at temperatures sufficient to enhance stress-assisted diffusion but insufficient to cause an independent thermal phase transformation.
The critical stress and secondary-phase volume fraction required for toughness loss vary with alloy composition and processing history.
The hypothesis is to be tested by comparing loaded and unloaded specimens taken from the same initially single-phase batch.
Failure to observe both a statistically significant increase in grain-boundary secondary phases and a measurable toughness reduction in loaded specimens is designated as the falsifying result.
